hook: Ever wondered why your Wi-Fi dies in the bathroom?
script: GUEST: [expr:0.4] Why does my signal drop the second I close the door?
HOST: [expr:0.7] Wi-Fi signals hate obstacles, especially thick walls and ceramic tiles.
GUEST: [expr:0.3] So the tile is blocking my internet feed?
HOST: [expr:0.6] Exactly, water in pipes and dense materials absorb those radio waves.
GUEST: [expr:0.4] Is there an easy way to fix that?
HOST: [expr:0.8] Move your router to a central, high spot in your home.

hook: Here is why crypto transactions take so long to process.
script: GUEST: [expr:0.4] Why do I have to wait for my crypto transfer?
HOST: [expr:0.7] Think of it like a huge line at a bank counter.
GUEST: [expr:0.3] So everyone is waiting for one teller?
HOST: [expr:0.6] Every node in the network needs to double check your transaction.
GUEST: [expr:0.4] That sounds like a total traffic jam.
HOST: [expr:0.8] It is, but it guarantees nobody can cheat the system.

hook: Why does restarting your computer fix almost every glitch?
script: GUEST: [expr:0.4] Why does rebooting actually work every single time?
HOST: [expr:0.7] Imagine your computer brain gets filled with messy sticky notes.
GUEST: [expr:0.3] And restarting just throws them all away?
HOST: [expr:0.6] Spot on, it completely clears your temporary RAM memory.
GUEST: [expr:0.4] So it gets a fresh clean slate?
HOST: [expr:0.8] Yes, giving software a clean place to start fresh.

hook: What actually happens when you delete a file forever?
script: GUEST: [expr:0.4] Is my file really gone when I hit delete?
HOST: [expr:0.7] Not right away, the computer just hides the pointer.
GUEST: [expr:0.3] So the actual data is still sitting there?
HOST: [expr:0.6] It marks that drive space as available for new stuff.
GUEST: [expr:0.4] When does it disappear for good then?
HOST: [expr:0.8] Only when new files write directly over top of it.

hook: How open source software builds the entire internet today.
script: GUEST: [expr:0.4] What makes open source code so special anyway?
HOST: [expr:0.7] It is like a global potluck recipe shared with everyone.
GUEST: [expr:0.3] Anyone can view and improve the recipe?
HOST: [expr:0.6] Thousands of developers work together to catch bugs fast.
GUEST: [expr:0.4] So free code can be super reliable?
HOST: [expr:0.8] Absolutely, it powers most of the servers on earth.
